newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX DOWN SHORT TERM BUT UPTREND TO STAY.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX DOWN SHORT TERM BUT UPTREND TO STAY.

text.p: NYMEX crude and products still remain firmly in technical uptrend with good trendline support in place to cushion the effects of fundamental pressure from Iraqi crude, analysts said.
Fenella Graham at MeesPierson said in her daily report, "We remain wary of any violent swings that unexpected Iraq news may bring and therefore still keep trading volumes light".

On the spot month continuation chart for NYMEX crude uptrend support rising from around $19 on July 22 and passing through July 31's $19.65 low comes in at around $20.15 today and continues to provide a solid base to the market.
Analysts say crude prices could start to edge higher from here once the fundamental effects of Iraqi crude sales have dissipated, though the market must hold $20 to do so.
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International said "The sloppy nature of Wednesday's weakness forces me to leave the door open for a final new high before I turn aggressively bearish".
A break of $20 could tip prices back through to $19 with little support in between. To the upside Tuesday's $20.94 remains the initial target on the way to the $22.40 high of May 16.

Also on the short term bearish side slow stochastics crossed at around 80 percent on Wednesday and an imperfect triple top around $20.93 formed by the price action of the past three days puts a hard top to the market.
The long legged near Doji candlestick formed as a result of Tuesday's price action where the open and close were close together could also be read as bearish.
To those who follow Japanese charting techniques the pattern represents a market that has lost its sense of direction.

Unleaded gasoline filled the gap down formed last week between July 31's low of 66.10 cents and August 1's high of 65.30 cents on Tuesday and has continued to edge higher, making fresh high ground over the past three days.

Though Thursday looks likely to provide some set-back to this pattern analysts say the market looks like staying wedged in an uptrend bounded by trendline support stemming from July 23's 59.50 cent low up through August 1's 62.40 cent low and longer term upside resistance from June 23 56.30 high which has capped the market over the past three days.
In contrast to gasoline's fresh daily highs heating oil is starting to show a bear flag formation.
After Monday's wide ranging day the market has traded progressively lower, though remains well above trendline support that comes in around 56.20 cents today.
